title: CEO Interview with Stephen Strausser of VON ARDENNE North America, Inc. - Semiwiki
gist: VON ARDENNE North America CEO Stephen Strausser describes the company's push into semiconductor advanced packaging and MEMS/PiezoMEMS thin-film deposition, launching the sub-nanometer-precision OPTA X300 coating platform and a new EUV-ready Dresden cleanroom, as shrinking, increasingly 3D transistor architectures push customers toward atomic-layer coating precision.

themes.theme: Thin-film deposition as a semiconductor bottleneck

insights.claim: Modern transistors require films only a few atomic layers thick with extremely tight thickness, composition, and conformality control, because shrinking devices, increasingly three-dimensional architectures, and new materials are making thin-film deposition one of the biggest challenges in semiconductor manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: Deposition-equipment precision is becoming a gating factor for next-generation transistor yield, favoring vendors who can hit atomic-layer-level tolerances over commodity coating-tool suppliers.
insights.quote: today’s transistors require films that are only a few atomic layers thick with extremely tight thickness, composition and conformality control.
insights.locator: For example, today's transistors require films

insights.claim: Small variations in thin-film thickness or composition can reduce chip performance and yield, and poor coating of deep trenches, vias, and 3D structures leads to defects and electrical failures that are costly for chipmakers.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: Coating-related defects in 3D device structures are a direct yield-loss driver, making deposition-tool selection a material cost lever for fabs moving to advanced packaging and 3D architectures.
insights.locator: In addition, these devices have deep trenches

insights.claim: VON ARDENNE differentiates from deposition-equipment competitors by offering custom-engineered, configure-to-order vacuum deposition systems rather than standardized platforms, aiming to solve advanced coating challenges that conventional vendors won't address.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: A custom-engineering positioning targets complex, low-volume/high-value coating problems that standardized-platform competitors avoid, a differentiated niche rather than a scale/commodity play.
insights.quote: solve advanced coating challenges that conventional vendors won’t address

insights.claim: VON ARDENNE serves semiconductor advanced packaging, MEMS, and PiezoMEMS applications, alongside aerospace coatings for turbine components, optical systems, aviation transparencies, and space optics, building on decades of experience as a coating-equipment leader in the glass and photovoltaics industries.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: Diversification across semiconductor, aerospace, and legacy glass/photovoltaics markets reduces VON ARDENNE's dependence on any single end market's capex cycle.
insights.locator: In the semiconductor industry, we advance high-precision

insights.claim: VON ARDENNE provides lifecycle support including upgrades for legacy 200mm fab equipment, spare parts, and process improvements to extend equipment life and performance.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: A lifecycle-support/upgrade business model creates a recurring revenue stream tied to installed 200mm fab base, independent of new leading-edge tool sales.

insights.claim: VON ARDENNE introduced its OPTA X300 rotary disk coating system, a sub-nanometer-precision deposition platform purpose-built for electrical and optical layers used in memory, photonics, and sensor devices, supporting customers from R&D through high-volume manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: The OPTA X300 is VON ARDENNE's flagship deposition platform launch, a concrete product to track for adoption among memory, photonics, and sensor manufacturers.
insights.locator: At SEMICON West 2025, we introduced our new OPTA X300

insights.claim: VON ARDENNE opened a new cleanroom in Dresden, Germany with 200 square meters of ISO 5 (Class 100) assembly/test space featuring airborne molecular contamination control, plus 400 square meters of ISO 7 manufacturing space, designed to be extreme ultraviolet (EUV)-ready for semiconductor, optical, and space applications.
insights.speaker: Stephen Strausser
insights.so_what: New EUV-ready cleanroom capacity signals VON ARDENNE is investing ahead of demand for leading-edge and space-grade coating work, a capacity expansion worth tracking for delivery lead-time impact on customers.
insights.locator: The new cleanroom in Dresden, Germany
